summary: ignisGuard is an interactive platform that harmonizes over 20 years of heat-source detections from the MODIS and VIIRS satellite sensors (NASA FIRMS) into a unified timeline, enabling the analysis of historical fire patterns in Argentina and the anticipation of emergencies.
details:
IgnisGuard is an ecological intelligence platform that monitors and analyzes wildfire patterns across Argentina by unifying over 20 years of fragmented NASA FIRMS satellite data into a single interactive interface.

How It Works

  • Data Harmonization Pipeline: Raw MODIS (~1 km) and VIIRS (~375 m) hotspot detections are ingested, deduplicated across historical (SP) and near real-time (NRT) products, converted from UTC to local Argentine calendar days (UTC-3), and mapped onto a standardized Uber H3 hexagonal grid (~0.7 km² cells) across 7 key Argentine ecological regions.
  • Backend & Storage: Aggregated data is stored in Parquet and MySQL (fire_cell_day and region_day tables) and served via a FastAPI backend that also supports on-demand background updates directly from the UI.
  • Interactive Frontend: Users explore hotspots on a custom 3D globe, browse a 20-year × 12-month regional heatmap, and compare current activity against two decades of baseline data using an "On This Day" historical view.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Higher Confidence: Cross-referencing MODIS and VIIRS detections within the same H3 cell highlights multi-sensor agreement as a built-in reliability signal, helping filter out false positives.
  • Faster Decision-Making: Researchers, responders, and policymakers can distinguish routine seasonal burns from anomalous wildfire outbreaks without needing GIS expertise or manual data cleaning.

Tech Stack

  • Backend & Data: Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, MySQL 8, pandas, GeoPandas, H3, PyArrow, Docker.
  • Frontend: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, and a custom HTML5 2D Canvas rendering engine for the 3D globe (built from scratch without MapLibre or D3).
  • Data Sources: NASA FIRMS satellite telemetry (MODIS & VIIRS).

Creativity & Key Considerations

Instead of discarding overlapping multi-satellite detections as duplicate noise, IgnisGuard turns MODIS+VIIRS overlap into a visual confidence halo on a lightweight, dependency-free 2D Canvas globe. Key engineering considerations included resolving UTC-to-local day splitting, harmonizing differing sensor resolutions, pre-aggregating data for sub-second historical queries, and handling loading, error, and empty states cleanly across the UI.
